exposure: Birth asphyxia (8 min intrauterine clamping of the umbilical cord)
Oral plasma supplementation (maternal plasma or water in milk replacer)
cohort: The study participants were Cesarean-delivered near-term pigs.
finding: Birth asphyxia in pigs led to immediate disturbance of electrolyte balance, impaired fluid retention, and kidney impairments, but plasma feeding improved postnatal newborn hydration and kidney condition following asphyxia.
